item.title: November 2026 Redding Rental Market Update for Property Owners
item.description: Redding rental market update for November 2026: 93.1% occupancy, 32 days listed to leased, renewals, rents, and a Thanksgiving thank-you.
item.content:encoded:
A Thanksgiving message, an update on Redding's rental market, a January listing-photo rule, and holiday dates around town.

November in Redding brings shorter days, the first real rain, and the arrival of the downtown Christmas tree at Market and Yuba.


�� A Heartfelt Thanksgiving Thank You


This time of year, Joline and I always stop to count our blessings. Every year, we land on the same one: you.


To every property owner who trusts us with your homes and investments, thank you . You did not just hand us a set of keys. You trusted us with something you worked hard to build, and we never take that lightly.


To every resident who calls one of our homes their home, thank you . You make our neighborhoods what they are, and we are honored to be part of your story here in Redding.


We have met so many great people along the way. Owners who became friends, residents who have been with us for years, and vendors and partners who show up for this community every single day. Those relationships are the best part of what we do, and they are the reason we love coming to work.


From our family to yours, we are truly, deeply grateful. Happy Thanksgiving.


- Aaron and Joline


��️ Redding Rental Market Update


Here is what we are seeing across the 1,022 rental units Authority Property Management manages in Redding and Shasta County .


Occupancy is holding strong. As of November 10, our portfolio is 93.1% occupied, up from 92.8% in September. Of the 71 vacant units, 12 already have a signed lease and are waiting on move-in day.


Residents are staying. In October, 22 residents renewed their leases, and 7 out of 10 residents who reached a renewal decision chose to stay. Renewing residents saw an average rent increase of about 2.4%. That steady, modest increase keeps good residents in place and protects your income without the cost of a turnover.


Homes are moving. We moved in 27 new residents in October against 20 move-outs, and we received more than 230 rental inquiries in that one month. Homes we leased in October went from listed to leased in about 32 days on average, faster than the 36.5 days we averaged in September. Our leasing team also answered nearly 98% of incoming calls from prospective residents. Demand for well-priced, well-kept homes in Redding remains healthy.


Here is what rent looks like across our portfolio today (average current rent, occupied homes):


  • 2-bedroom: about $1,289
  • 3-bedroom: about $1,902
  • 4-bedroom and larger: about $2,328


These are averages across all leases, including long-time residents, so new leases on updated homes often come in higher. Pricing a home correctly from day one is still the single biggest factor in how fast it leases.


What this means for owners and investors: with sales slowing and more homes sitting on the market, a well-managed rental continues to be a strong option. If you own a home that has not sold, or you are weighing a new investment, start with a free rental analysis . We will show you what it should rent for, based on the homes we lease every week.


�� Shasta County Sales Market Snapshot


Local agent Josh Barker reports that Shasta County closings fell 33% in October compared with a year ago, while the median sale price rose 6.3% to $361,500. Active listings are up 2.9%, homes are averaging 106 days on market, and 30-year fixed rates sit near 7.24%. Fire insurance remains a real cost for owners, with the average Redding homeowner paying around $1,900 a year, so review your coverage at renewal with your insurance professional. Slower sales and longer market times are leading more sellers to consider renting.


⚖️ Legislative Lowdown: AB 2025 Listing-Photo Disclosure


Starting January 1, 2027, Assembly Bill 2025 adds Civil Code section 1940.11 . If a rental ad uses a digitally altered image, including AI-generated images or photos edited to change furniture, flooring, paint, landscaping, or views, the ad needs a reasonably conspicuous disclosure on or next to the image, plus the unaltered photo or a link, URL, or QR code to a public site that clearly identifies the original. Ordinary lighting, cropping, or color corrections that do not change how the property is represented are not covered. If you virtually stage a listing or clean up a yard in software, plan to label it and keep a path to the real photo.


This section is informational only and is not legal advice. Owners should review this with their attorney or trusted professional when needed.


��️ Seasonal Maintenance Tips


The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency puts it simply: the key to mold control is moisture control. If wet or damp materials are dried within 24 to 48 hours, in most cases mold will not grow. Before the heavier rains:


  • Clear gutters and downspouts, and check the roof for loose or missing shingles
  • Check under sinks, behind toilets, and around the water heater for slow leaks
  • Wrap exposed pipes and freeze-prone hose bibs before cold nights
  • Ask residents to report stains, drips, or musty odors early


�� Ask the Expert


Q: My home has been on the market and is not selling. Should I rent it instead?


Maybe. It depends on your payment, your timeline, and what the home could realistically rent for. Start with current rent comps and a clear look at expenses, including insurance. A free rental analysis is an easy first step. Then talk with your tax and legal professionals about your own situation.


�� Holiday Season Around Redding


A few local dates to enjoy with your family this season:


  • The nearly 80-foot downtown Christmas tree, donated by Sierra Pacific Industries, arrived November 8 at Market and Yuba.
  • The Turkey Trot is Thanksgiving morning, November 26, at Diestelhorst Landing.
  • Redding Garden of Lights at Turtle Bay runs November 20, 2026, through January 3, 2027, with a new Christkindl Market. Closed November 30 through December 1, December 7 through 8, and December 14 through 15.
  • Tree lighting Friday, December 4, at 7 PM during First Friday downtown. Lighted Christmas Parade Saturday, December 5, 6 to 8:30 PM downtown, hosted by the Active 20-30 Club. Jingle Bell Fun Run December 5 at 4 PM at Turtle Bay.


�� We're Always Here to Help


Whether you are prepping for winter or deciding between selling and renting, we are here to help.


At Authority Property Management , We Make Rentals Simple .

Website: www.authoritypm.com

item.title: Five Questions to Ask Before Hiring a Redding Property Manager (And Five Things They Should Report Monthly)
item.description: Hiring a Redding property manager? Ask these 5 essential questions upfront and make sure these 5 items show up in your owner reporting every single month.
item.content:encoded:
The right questions before you sign a management agreement, paired with clear monthly reporting once you do, will tell you everything you need to know about who is watching your rental.

A Good Sales Pitch Is Easy. Month-After-Month Accountability Is What Protects Your Rental.

If you own a rental home in Redding , Anderson , Shasta Lake , Cottonwood , or anywhere in Shasta County , handing over the keys to a property manager is a big step. You are trusting someone else with a major financial asset, your monthly cash flow, and the people living under your roof.


Most property management interviews sound great in the conference room. Every company will tell you they screen tenants carefully, answer the phone, and treat your house like their own. The real difference shows up in two places: the specifics they are willing to put in writing before you hire them, and the numbers and documentation they send you every month after you sign.


Joline and I have each held our California real estate licenses since 2005, giving us more than 42 years of combined experience in this business. When we started Authority Property Management here in Redding in 2015, we built our systems around a simple idea: owners should never have to guess what they are paying for or what is happening at their property.


Whether you are interviewing your first manager or wondering if your current one is really doing the job, this two-part guide covers the five questions to ask before you sign and the five things your property manager should be reporting to you every single month.

Note: This article shares general educational information for California rental owners, not legal, tax, or accounting advice.

 

Part 1: Five Questions to Ask Before Hiring a Property Manager

We shared a short starter list in an earlier post on interviewing a local management company. When you are ready to dig deeper into how a manager actually operates day to day, these five questions will separate clear, well-run operations from vague sales pitches.

 

1. Are You a Licensed California Real Estate Broker, and How Do You Handle Trust Funds?

In California, property management is not an informal side business. Under California Business and Professions Code sections 10130 and 10131(b), leasing real property, negotiating leases, and collecting rents for others for compensation are licensed real estate activities that must be performed by, or under the supervision of, a licensed California real estate broker.


Before you hire anyone, look them up on the California Department of Real Estate's public license lookup . In less than a minute, you can verify the company's corporate license status, confirm who serves as the designated broker-officer, and check whether there is any disciplinary history on file. (For reference, Authority Property Management Inc. is licensed under CA DRE #01990823, with Aaron Robertson and Joline Robertson serving as licensed California real estate brokers.)


Then ask a follow-up question: Where does my rent money sit between the day the tenant pays and the day I get paid?

Under California Business and Professions Code section 10145, rents and security deposits collected on behalf of property owners are trust funds. They belong to the beneficiary, not the management company, and must be held in a properly designated trust bank account and reconciled regularly. A professional manager will explain their trust accounting clearly and without hesitation.

 

2. Is Your Pricing Published Upfront, and What Happens When My Rental Is Vacant?

If you have to give up your phone number and sit through a 30-minute sales call just to find out what a company charges, pause and ask why.


When you interview a property manager, ask for the full fee schedule upfront:

  • What is the monthly management percentage, and is there a monthly minimum?
  • What is the tenant placement fee when a new resident moves in, and do you charge anything until the home is actually rented?
  • Do you charge a monthly management fee while the property is sitting vacant between tenants?
  • What does a lease renewal cost when a good resident stays another year?


We believe owners deserve to see every number before they ever pick up the phone. That is why we publish our placement-only and full-service packages right on our residential property management pricing page. And if your property is vacant, we do not charge a monthly management fee while it sits empty.

 

3. Do You Mark Up Maintenance Invoices, and What Is Your Repair Approval Limit?

Maintenance is where a lot of owners get burned by surprise bills. Some management companies add a percentage surcharge on top of what the plumber, electrician, or handyman charges. Others dispatch expensive work without ever letting the owner know until the money is already gone from the monthly check.


Ask three plain questions before you sign:


  • Do you add any markup to vendor invoices? At Authority Property Management, the answer is no. You pay what our vetted, licensed, and insured local vendors charge, and we pass the invoice straight through to you.
  • What is the dollar limit before you contact me for approval? You want a manager who can handle a small leaking flapper right away without bothering you at work, while still checking with you before approving a larger non-emergency bill. On our plans, we handle routine repairs under $500 promptly to protect the home and contact you for approval before moving forward on non-emergency repairs over $500.
  • Who answers the 2:00 a.m. emergency call? Make sure there is a real 24/7 emergency maintenance process so your resident is never left with running water in the middle of the night.

 

4. How Do You Show Vacant Properties and Screen Applicants?

Leaving a vacant Redding rental on an unmonitored lockbox is a shortcut that can invite trouble. Ask how prospective renters actually tour your property and who verifies their identity.


Our local team prefers face-to-face showings with a dedicated showing representative who meets prospective renters at the home, answers questions, and makes sure the property is locked up afterward. For pre-screened renters who need extra scheduling flexibility, we also offer a secure digital lockbox option that requires ID verification and pre-screening before anyone gets access.


On the screening side, ask what the company checks and how they stay compliant with federal and California fair housing laws. Every adult applicant should go through a consistent, written screening process covering credit, income verification, and rental history, applied equally to every applicant. You can read more about how our leasing and screening workflow runs on our property management services page.

 

5. What Is Your Exact Owner Payout Schedule, and Can I See a Sample Monthly Statement?

Cash flow timing matters, especially if you have a mortgage, property taxes, or insurance drafting out of your bank account each month. Ask the manager to walk you through the monthly calendar from the day rent is due to the day funds land in your account.


For example, our schedule is built to be predictable every month: tenant rent is collected between the 1st and the 5th, vendor invoices for completed work are processed, and owner payouts are disbursed on the 18th of each month via direct deposit.


Before you wrap up the interview, ask to see a sample monthly owner statement. That sample leads straight into the second half of what every Shasta County rental owner should expect.

 

Part 2: Five Things Your Property Manager Should Be Reporting Monthly

Hiring the right team is step one. Step two is making sure you get clear, complete information every month without having to chase anyone down. Here are the five essentials your property manager should be reporting monthly.

 

1. Rent Collected, Payment Status, and Exact Owner Disbursements

Your monthly statement should never read like a puzzle. At a glance, you should be able to see:


  • The full rent amount billed for the month and the date it was collected
  • Any additional tenant charges collected, such as pet rent or late fees
  • The management fee deducted for that period
  • The exact net disbursement sent to your bank account, with the date and reference number


Just as important, if a tenant has not paid by the end of the grace period, you should not find out by noticing an empty bank account on payout day. Your manager should keep you informed early about late payments, communication with the resident, and any legal notices served under California law.

 

2. Itemized Maintenance Expenses Backed by Actual Vendor Invoices

A single line on a statement that says "$385.00 - Maintenance" is not enough. You deserve to know what broke, who fixed it, and what the vendor actually billed.

Every month, when a repair is completed at your property, your reporting packet should include the itemized transaction along with a copy of the work order and the paid vendor invoice. Seeing the actual vendor bill does two important jobs for you:


  • It confirms you are paying the true vendor cost with zero hidden markups.
  • It gives you and your tax preparer clean, organized documentation when it is time to file your year-end tax return alongside your annual summary and 1099.

 

3. Your Property's Separate Trust Ledger and Reserve Balance

Because owner funds in California are held in trust, your monthly statement should show more than just this month's rent minus this month's bills. It should show the continuous financial picture for your specific property.


In its October 2026 compliance guidance on trust fund records , the California Department of Real Estate highlights the three core records required under Business and Professions Code section 10145 and Commissioner's Regulations 2831 , 2831.1, and 2831.2: a chronological control record for the trust account, a separate record for each beneficiary showing every deposit, disbursement, and running balance, and a monthly trust account reconciliation against the bank statement.


On your end as the owner, that clean accounting shows up in your monthly statement and inside our 24/7 online owner statement portal . You can log in anytime from your phone or computer to see your beginning balance, every transaction in and out, and your ending reserve balance.

 

4. Inspection Updates and Proactive Property Preservation Notes

Your bank ledger only tells half the story. The physical condition of your roof, plumbing, HVAC system, landscaping, and interior is what protects your long-term equity here in Northern California. Whenever a drive-by check, annual interior inspection, or maintenance visit turns up something worth watching, it should be reported to you promptly. That includes:


  • Early warning signs like slow drainage, worn supply lines, fence wear, or gutter buildup ahead of Redding's fall and winter rains
  • Follow-up notes confirming how the resident is caring for the home
  • Recommendations for routine preventative care before a small fix turns into an expensive emergency


Good reporting keeps you ahead of repairs instead of reacting to them after the damage is done.

 

5. Upcoming Lease Expirations, Renewal Plans, and Local Market Rent Checks

Your property manager should never wait until the final week of a lease to ask what you want to do next.

In the months leading up to a lease expiration, your monthly updates should flag the upcoming end date, review the tenant's payment and care track record, and compare your current rent against what similar homes in Redding, Anderson, Shasta Lake, or Cottonwood are actually leasing for today.


In California, timing matters for legal compliance too. Many residential rentals are subject to the statewide rent-increase caps and just-cause rules under the Tenant Protection Act (AB 1482, codified in Civil Code sections 1947.12 and 1946.2), as well as the 30-day and 90-day written notice rules for rent increases under Civil Code section 827. You can review how those state rules work on the California Attorney General's landlord-tenant resource page . Flagging renewals early gives you time to make a smart, compliant decision and keep a great resident in place.


If you are currently managing a rental on your own and want to know how your rent compares to today's Shasta County market, you can request a free rental analysis from our team anytime.

 

Wrap Up

Choosing a property manager comes down to trust, and trust is built on clear answers and clean numbers.


Before you hire a company, ask about their California broker license and trust accounting, their published fees, their maintenance markup and approval rules, their showing and screening process, and their payout calendar. Once they are on the job, expect monthly reporting that shows your rent collection, actual vendor invoices, trust ledger balances, property condition updates, and upcoming lease plans.


If you would like to see how our team handles owner reporting or talk through what your rental needs, give us a call. We are always happy to answer your questions with zero pressure.

 

At Authority Property Management , We Make Rentals Simple .

Website: www.authoritypm.com

item.title: Is Your Redding Rental Properly Insured Before Storm Season?
item.description: Before storm season hits Redding, review your rental insurance with your agent: landlord policies, slow leaks, mold, 60-day vacancy, and lost rent.
item.content:encoded:
Before winter rain tests your roof and plumbing, a fifteen-minute review with your insurance agent can help you spot common policy gaps on a rental home.

The Worst Time to Read Your Insurance Policy Is After the Ceiling Drips.


Fall in Redding always brings a shift. One week you are running the air conditioner in the afternoon, and the next week rain is in the forecast and leaves are collecting in the gutters.


Most rental owners remember to check the roof, clear the downspouts, and service the heater before winter settles in. Far fewer pull out their insurance declarations page to make sure the policy on file actually matches how the property is being used today.


**We are property managers, not insurance agents or attorneys, so nothing in this post is coverage or legal advice.


Every policy is a contract with its own definitions, limits, endorsements, and exclusions. Still, after Joline and I have each spent more than 20 years licensed in California real estate, with over 42 years of combined experience helping owners around Shasta County , we have seen where surprises tend to happen when bad weather arrives.


Here is a plain checklist of topics and questions to bring to your licensed insurance agent or broker before the wet season is in full swing.

 

1. Is the Home Insured as a Rental or Still on a Homeowners Policy?

This question comes up often with accidental landlords. Maybe you lived in your Redding or Anderson home for years, moved into a new place, and decided to rent out the first house instead of selling. Or maybe you inherited a family home and placed a resident in it.


When a house transitions from your primary residence to a tenant-occupied rental, the risk profile changes. Standard homeowners coverage is written for an owner who lives on the premises. If you move out and rent the property to tenants without updating your policy to landlord or dwelling coverage, you do not want to find out during a claim that your policy was only written for an owner-occupied home.


If you are turning a home you used to live in into a rental this fall, starting with a free rental analysis and a quick call to your insurance agent will help you get both the numbers and the coverage lined up from day one.


Questions to ask your insurance agent:

  • Does my current policy reflect that this property is tenant-occupied rather than owner-occupied?
  • If I have an umbrella policy or hold the rental in an LLC or trust, is the named insured listed accurately across every policy?

 

2. Sudden Water Damage vs. Slow Seepage, Leaks, and Mold

Winter storms and older plumbing test a rental home in two very different ways: all at once, or drop by drop.

In the California Department of Insurance Residential Insurance Guide , the state breaks down perils that are typically covered by a standard homeowners policy and perils that are generally not covered. While windstorm damage and "sudden & accidental water damage" appear on the typically covered list, the guide notes that standard policies generally do not cover:


  • Water damage caused by seepage or leaks
  • Mold
  • Wear and tear or maintenance
  • Flood and earth movement


That distinction matters in the real world. A sudden, accidental pipe burst or a tree limb punching through a roof in a windstorm is very different from roof flashing that has been weeping slowly into an attic for months, or a slow drip under a kitchen sink that nobody reported until the cabinet floor softened and mold appeared. Surface flooding from heavy runoff is also separate from standard water damage coverage and typically requires a separate flood policy, such as through the National Flood Insurance Program.


Because slow leaks, maintenance issues, and mold are commonly excluded or strictly limited, your best protection against slow water damage is operational: routine inspections, clear resident communication so small drips get reported right away, and prompt repairs with licensed vendors before a minor leak becomes a habitability issue.


Questions to ask your insurance agent:

  • How does my rental policy define sudden and accidental water damage versus slow seepage or repeated leakage?
  • Is mold excluded outright on my policy, or is there a limited endorsement when mold results from a covered water loss?
  • What maintenance records or inspection documentation does the insurer expect if a storm or water claim ever arises?

 

3. The 60-Day Vacancy Rule During Fall and Winter Turnovers

Late fall and winter are naturally slower months for leasing across Redding, Shasta Lake, and Cottonwood. Sometimes an owner also holds a house empty between residents to remodel a kitchen, replace flooring, or wait out the holidays.


Before you let a rental sit empty for an extended stretch, check your policy's vacancy clause. The California Department of Insurance guide lists losses to a house vacant for 60 days or more among the perils generally not covered by a standard residential policy. Policies can restrict or suspend certain coverages once a building sits unoccupied past the number of days stated in the contract, because an empty house has nobody inside to spot a leak, a break-in, or a heater issue early.


We recently walked through what an empty fall rental really costs Redding owners in lost rent and daily carrying bills like utilities and yard care. Insurance is one more reason a long vacancy needs your attention.


Questions to ask your insurance agent:

  • How many days can my rental sit vacant or unoccupied before coverage restrictions kick in?
  • How does my policy distinguish between "vacant" and "unoccupied," and does an active renovation change what is covered?
  • If the home will be empty for an extended remodel or turnover, do I need a vacancy permit or a builder's risk endorsement?

 

4. Loss of Rents (Fair Rental Value) and Rebuilding Limits

When a covered fire or severe windstorm damages a rental home badly enough that your resident cannot safely live there during repairs, fixing the structure is only half of the financial equation. Your mortgage, property taxes, and insurance bills keep arriving even when rent stops.


In the California Department of Insurance Commercial Insurance Guide , the department explains "Time Element" coverages, noting that loss of rents and rental value cover loss of rental income to the property owner caused by damage or destruction of a building rendering it unfit for occupancy. On residential landlord policies, this is often called Loss of Rents or Fair Rental Value coverage.


At the same time, the state's residential guide reminds owners that your dwelling limit should reflect what it would actually cost in labor and materials to rebuild the structure, not the original purchase price or current real estate market value. It also highlights two other details that catch owners off guard after a major loss: whether the policy pays Replacement Cost or Actual Cash Value (which deducts for physical depreciation on partial losses), and whether the policy includes Building Code Upgrade (ordinance or law) coverage if local codes have changed since the home was built.


Questions to ask your insurance agent:

  • Does my policy include Loss of Rents (or Fair Rental Value) coverage if a covered loss makes the rental uninhabitable?
  • What is the dollar cap and maximum number of months for that lost-rent coverage, and does it match what the home actually rents for today?
  • Is my dwelling coverage written for Replacement Cost or Actual Cash Value , and does it include ordinance or law coverage for building code upgrades?

 

5. Tenant Belongings, Renters Insurance, and Additional Insureds

Two final items are worth clearing up before storm season, because they prevent misunderstandings with your residents and your management team.


First, a landlord's property policy covers the building, not the resident's furniture, clothing, or electronics. As the California Department of Insurance states plainly in its residential guide: "Your landlord does not provide insurance for your personal property." If a covered fire or windstorm damages a rental, the tenant looks to their own renters insurance policy for their personal belongings, temporary living expenses (loss of use), and personal liability. Setting clear expectations in the lease about renters insurance helps protect both the resident and the owner.


Second, if you work with a property management company, check how your manager is listed on the policy. Many owners hear "additional interest" and "additional insured" and assume they mean the same thing. As we explain in our guide on adding your property manager as an additional insured , an additional interest typically only receives policy notices, whereas naming your property manager as an additional insured helps align liability protection between the owner and the company managing the home day to day.


Questions to ask your insurance agent:

  • Does my policy have any specific requirements regarding tenant liability or renters insurance?
  • Is my property management company properly listed as an additional insured on my rental dwelling policy?

 

Wrap Up

You do not need to become an insurance underwriter to protect your Redding rental . You just need to ask the right questions before the weather turns, and put what you learn in writing. In fact, the California Department of Insurance specifically recommends documenting your coverage discussions and inquiries with your agent or broker in writing so everyone is on the same page at renewal time.


Pair a solid policy review with good day-to-day habits: keep roofs and gutters clear, encourage residents to report small leaks the day they spot them, and handle maintenance before minor water intrusion turns into an excluded repair.

﻿

We help rental owners across Redding, Anderson, Shasta Lake, Cottonwood, Palo Cedro, and Shasta County keep a close eye on their properties year-round. You can see how our team handles routine inspections, 24/7 maintenance coordination with vetted local vendors, and lease management on our property management services page, or give us a call anytime.


At Authority Property Management , We Make Rentals Simple .

item.title: Halloween Decorating Tips That Protect Your Security Deposit
item.description: Decorating your Redding rental for Halloween or the holidays? Use these damage-free hanging, lighting, and yard tips to protect your security deposit.
item.content:encoded:
Putting up Halloween and holiday decorations is part of making a house feel like home, and a few simple habits will keep your rental looking festive without risking damage or security deposit deductions later

Festive Porch, Full Deposit: How to Decorate Your Rental Without Leaving a Mark.


Driving through neighborhoods in Redding, Anderson, Shasta Lake, and Cottonwood in late October is one of the best parts of fall. Porch pumpkins, string lights, and creative yard displays make a street feel welcoming and lived in.


We love seeing residents enjoy the season and make the house they rent feel like home. Unlike an HOA with a thick binder of seasonal mandates, we do not hand out a list of special lease rules for Halloween or Christmas decorations. Instead, we always encourage good neighbor etiquette and smart, damage-free decorating habits so you can enjoy the holidays now without running into repair charges against your security deposit when you eventually move out.


Under California law, as summarized on the California Attorney General's landlord-tenant resource page , a security deposit cannot be used for ordinary wear and tear, but it can be used to repair damage beyond normal wear and tear caused by a resident or their guests. The good news is that almost every common holiday decorating mishap is easy to avoid with a few simple swaps.

 

1. Hang Indoor Cobwebs, Wreaths, and Lights Without Peeling the Paint

Interior drywall and painted trim are the number one place where holiday decorations leave an expensive footprint. Heavy-duty mounting tape, cheap novelty window clings, and thumbtacks can pull paint right down to the drywall paper or leave stained residue when the weather warms up.

Here is how to keep walls, doors, and windows clean:


  • Use removable damage-free hooks and pull the tab slowly. When taking down removable adhesive strips, always pull the tab straight down along the wall rather than yanking it toward you, which tears the paint.
  • Use over-the-door wreath hangers with a felt backing. Metal hooks work great on front and interior doors as long as they have a soft felt strip on the back so they do not scrape the top edge of the door paint every time it opens.
  • Skip duct tape, packaging tape, and hot glue on painted surfaces. Even a few days of sun on a window frame can bake standard tape adhesive onto vinyl or painted wood.
  • Test window clings on a small corner first. Some brightly colored gel clings can stain porous sills or painted wood trim if moisture condenses on the glass overnight.

 

2. Protect Roof Shingles, Fascia Boards, and Stucco Outside

When stringing orange lights for Halloween or transitioning into holiday lights next month, the biggest risk to the exterior of a home comes from staple guns, nails, and screws driven into the roof edge or siding. Puncturing roof shingles or flashing creates tiny entry points for water just as Redding's November and December rainstorms arrive. Nails and staples driven into wood fascia or stucco also leave chipped holes that require patching and painting later.


  • Use plastic gutter clips or shingle tabs instead of staples or nails. Plastic light clips slide onto rain gutters or under the front edge of a shingle without piercing anything, and they pop right off in January.
  • Never walk on tile or wet composition roofs. Beyond the personal safety risk, walking on roof tiles can crack them and lead to winter roof leaks.
  • Wrap porch railings and columns with zip ties or soft twine. Zip ties hold garlands, skeletons, and light strands securely in the wind without scratching the paint.

 

3. Watch for Sprinklers, Underground Lines, and Lawn Health in the Yard

Inflatables, tombstones, and yard stakes are fun for trick-or-treaters, but they can be hard on grass and irrigation systems if they stay in one spot too long.


  • Keep yard stakes shallow and away from sprinkler heads. Before pushing plastic or metal stakes into the lawn, check where the sprinkler heads and drip lines run so you do not puncture a PVC pipe or poly tubing underground.
  • Put inflatables on a timer and move heavy props occasionally. A large inflatable lying flat on damp grass all day blocks sunlight and traps moisture, which can leave a yellow dead patch in the lawn within a week.
  • Set carved pumpkins on a tray or porch mat. Real jack-o'-lanterns soften quickly in warm Northern California afternoons. Setting them on a plate or mat prevents rotting pumpkin juice from staining concrete steps or wood decking, and prevents mold from drawing pests to the front door.

 

4. Keep Walkways, Electrical Cords, and Porch Lights Safe for Visitors

Good holiday etiquette also means thinking about the neighbors, delivery drivers, and kids walking up your driveway after dark. According to the National Fire Protection Association's Halloween Fire Safety Tips , dried fall props like cornstalks, crepe paper, and fabric ghosts catch fire quickly when placed too close to heat sources.


  • Swap real candle flames for battery-operated LED tea lights. Battery candles inside jack-o'-lanterns and porch luminaries flicker just like the real thing without the fire risk around long costumes or dry leaves.
  • Use outdoor-rated extension cords and GFCI outlets. Never run indoor extension cords out through a pinched window screen or across a wet walkway where someone can trip.
  • Keep steps, handrails, and house numbers clear. Make sure trick-or-treaters and guests have a wide, well-lit path to the front door with no fake spiderwebs or cords stretched across face or ankle height.
  • Check your smoke and carbon monoxide alarms. Before plugging in seasonal lights and turning on the heater for the season, take thirty seconds to test your alarms. You can read more in our rental fire safety and smoke detector guide .

 

5. Be a Thoughtful Neighbor When the Night Winds Down

Part of living in a great neighborhood is looking out for the people next door. If your display includes motion-activated sound effects, strobe lights, or blower motors on yard inflatables, setting them on an evening timer so they turn off at a reasonable hour keeps the peace with neighbors who have sleeping kids, pets, or early work shifts. And once the holiday wraps up, taking decorations down in a timely manner keeps the neighborhood looking sharp and prevents fall winds and rain from tearing props loose or blowing them down the street.

��If you notice an exterior outlet that is not working properly, a loose porch railing, or a dark walkway light while setting up, let our team know through the online maintenance request portal so we can get it taken care of before guests arrive.

 

Wrap Up

You do not need a complicated rulebook to enjoy Halloween and the upcoming holiday season in a rental home. A little common sense, damage-free clips instead of nails and tape, battery candles instead of open flames, and consideration for your neighbors can help you enjoy the season while protecting your security deposit.

item.title: October 2026 Redding Rental Market Update for Property Owners
item.description: Before selling a Redding rental, owners should weigh taxes, depreciation, capital gains, 1031 options, and tenant risks to make a thoughtful hold-or-sell decision.
item.content:encoded:
Rates jump, accidental landlords arrive, and Redding rentals head into the rainy season. Here is what it means for your rental.

Introduction

October in Redding means cooler mornings, the first real rain on the way, and pumpkin patches popping up around town. It is also a month when the rental and sales markets start telling two different stories.


This month we cover our September numbers, a new kind of owner we are meeting more often, a jump in mortgage rates , a stove and refrigerator rule that is now in full swing, a quick winter-prep list, and a few ways we gave back in September.


��️ Redding Rental Market Update

Our portfolio vacancy is holding steady at about 6% as of October 11.

September was a busy month for our team:

  • 28 move-ins
  • 16 move-outs
  • 60 lease renewals

Sixty renewals tell us a lot of good residents are choosing to stay, and that is the best outcome for any owner. Every renewal is a month with no turnover costs and no empty home.


��Vacancies are ticking up a little, and we think we know why. More homes are entering the rental market , which brings us to this month's big topic.


�� Owner Insight: The Rise of the Accidental Landlord

We are meeting a lot of new owners right now. Many had a home for sale for a couple of months and could not get it sold. Now they want to rent it instead, and many are likely paying two mortgages while they wait. Many of them are also not willing to give up a great mortgage rate somewhere between 2% and 4%. We understand that. A rate like that is hard to walk away from. That extra inventory is a big reason vacancies are creeping up slightly in Redding.


So what is an accidental landlord ? It is someone who ends up renting out a home because of their situation, not because they set out to invest. Common reasons:

  • Moving for a new job
  • Buying a new home, planning to sell the old one, and then not being able to
  • Moving to a bigger city for better medical care during a life event


Most plan to rent for a few years. In our experience, most accidental landlords end up staying long-term landlords. They like the steady income, and they enjoy the tax benefits, especially depreciation. If you are new to that idea, our post on Rental Property Depreciation: Tax Deductions Every Landlord Should Know is a good place to start. As always, talk with your CPA about your own situation.


Know someone with a home that will not sell? Or are you in that spot yourself? We are happy to help. Start with a free rental analysis to see what the home could likely rent for.


�� Shasta County Sales Market Snapshot

In his October 2026 update, Josh Barker reports 30-year fixed rates around 7.75%, with some buyers seeing close to 8%. That is nearly a full point higher than a month or so ago. A buyer who qualified for about $400,000 last month may now qualify for closer to $360,000.


  • 208 homes sold in September, down about 9.2% from 229 a year earlier
  • Year-to-date, 2,100 sales versus 1,954 in 2025, still up about 7.5%
  • Homes are selling around 95% of original list price
  • Absorption is about 4.1 months, a balanced market


What it means for you: When payments jump, more households keep renting, which supports rental demand. It also means more homes that do not sell may turn into rentals. Clean, well-priced homes that are shown fast are more likely to lease first.


⚖️ Legislative Lowdown: AB 628 Is Now in Full Swing

A quick reminder. Under California Assembly Bill 628 , a working stove and a working refrigerator are now part of the basics a California rental must have (Civil Code Section 1941.1). It applies to leases entered into, amended, or extended on or after January 1, 2026. With renewals rolling in all year, it now covers a big share of homes.


  • The stove and fridge need to be in good working order
  • A recalled appliance does not count and needs to be repaired or replaced within 30 days of notice
  • A tenant can supply their own fridge, but only with specific written lease language


If a renewal is coming up on a home without appliances, let's plan for it now.


**This section is informational only and is not legal advice. Please review it with your attorney or trusted professional when needed.


��️ Seasonal Maintenance Tips

Redding can go from dry to drenched fast. A short fall checklist saves emergency calls later:


  • Service the heater and replace the filter before the first cold snap
  • Clear gutters and downspouts after the leaves drop
  • Look over the roof for loose or missing shingles
  • Wrap exposed pipes and hose bibs before freezing nights
  • Test smoke and CO alarms when daylight saving time ends on Sunday, November 1

 

�� Giving Back in September

September was a full month for our team in the community:

  • We sponsored and played in the Cronic Disaster Restoration Golf Fundraiser , with proceeds supporting Raising Shasta and the kids and families they serve across Shasta County.
  • We donated a raffle basket to Heroes on Paws , a benefit supporting local police K-9 units in Redding.


A big thank you to everyone who voted for us in the Best of the North State. Voting closed September 30, and we are truly grateful for every vote and kind word.


�� Fall Fun Around Redding

  • Redding Retro Halloween Night Market , Saturday, October 17, 6 to 9 PM, at 550 Cypress Ave
  • Downtown Fall Festival , Saturday, October 24, on Market Street, with a costume contest and downtown trick-or-treating from 3 to 6 PM
  • Hawes Haunts at Historic Hawes Farms, Friday and Saturday nights through October 31 (18+)


�� We're Always Here to Help

If you are prepping for winter, reviewing a renewal, or deciding between selling and renting, we are here to help.

At Authority Property Management , We Make Rentals Simple .

Website: www.authoritypm.com
